body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\), estimated by the raw \(\widehat\tau\).  Identification remains conditional on \texttt{ass:event-transport}.  The sharp conditional-risk and uniformly honest expected-length guarantees use \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\), respectively, and attach only to the subclass satisfying exactly the two strong full-design restrictions \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} and \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering}.  Under geometric \(\beta\)-mixing and marginal design-density bounds, uniform spacing contributes \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}=\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\); the rare-block obstruction makes this logarithm unavoidable without a sequential-overlap or other anti-clustering assumption, none of which is imposed.  The donor channel remains conditional on the assumed two-sided local modulus.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on the observed event state \(E_0\), each cohort contributes \(T\) exactly observed pre-event proxy paths with a density bounded above and away from zero; their calendar sequence is geometrically beta mixing.
sampling_model.units: At each pre-event path, cohort \(s\) supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded untreated wealth blocks, and the event date supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded treated wealth levels; event units need not be identically distributed.
sampling_model.treatment: The event occurs at \(t=0\). Consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and the maintained cross-date cohort-average event-transport equality identify the untreated finite-cohort event mean from the historical path regression.
sampling_model.overlap: The realized event path lies in an interior positive-probability region and every historical design density is bounded below there.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample of size \(N\) estimates only the event query and its unknown full heteroskedastic covariance. Historical training coordinates are exact. Fold-specific projected donor means, covariance spectral clipping, retained calendar blocks with fixed gaps, delete-block refits, separate exact Rademacher calibrations for calendar and event fluctuations, and a fourth-moment donor radius yield a total feasible procedure.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper derives identification and asymptotic-bias conditions for financial event-study estimators and explains that buy-and-hold comparisons require volatility matching.
The Holder repeated-measurement prediction rate has sparse order \((nm)^{-2s/(2s+d)}\) and dense order \(n^{-1}\), up to the stated logarithmic qualifications.
A local-polynomial Lepski procedure adapts pointwise to local design mass and local Holder smoothness under observed random design.
Theorem 1 expands local-linear regression with a generated covariate attached to every training observation through smoothed first-stage errors.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 establish deconvolution rates when latent training coordinates have replicated classical measurement error.
Theorems 7--8 evaluate a rate-optimal local-polynomial regression estimator at a sample-split estimated strongly convex minimizer.
The dependent-data theorem uses large-block--small-block coupling for conditional approximation of synthetic-control prediction error.
Spline and wavelet series estimators attain optimal uniform rates and functional normality under beta mixing and weak moments.
Ordered moduli characterize optimal confidence procedures for linear functionals over convex regression classes in a fixed Gaussian experiment.
The many-period--many-control result gives conditions for synthetic-control factor-loading recovery under imperfect pre-treatment fit.
The proximal synthetic-control theorems identify treatment effects by using excluded control outcomes as predetermined proxies.

body.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort average causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path. A maintained cross-date cohort-average transport restriction identifies it through the full historical wealth-path regression without event-date exchangeability. The raw generated-center local-polynomial estimator is exactly the event coefficient of an algebraic block-diagonal foldwise weighted least-squares panel regression on successful fits. Exact historical coordinates and an independently generated event center create treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, finite-spacing, and donor-modulus components. The smoothing term is present in the bookkeeping but never uniquely active; the sharp risk is the maximum of treated noise, path spacing, and \(N^{-\min\{\lambda,1\}}\) donor uncertainty. Matching lower bounds arise from joint panel laws on positive-probability query sets. A total retained-calendar-block interval combines observable Holder bias, separate exact Rademacher radii for calendar and event noise, and a fourth-moment donor-modulus allowance to attain the square-root expected-length frontier. Mean-only return-path information fails to identify compounded wealth by an explicit correlated-sign two-law witness, while the maintained full panel remains identifying.

project_justification.gap: Causal financial event-study theory treats mainly linear return contrasts, repeated-measurement regression fixes the query, generated-regressor theory moves every training coordinate, and synthetic-control intervals do not derive a generated-proxy minimax frontier for compounded wealth.
project_justification.niche: Many event studies observe historical proxy paths exactly, replicate untreated wealth blocks at each calendar window, and synthesize only the event-date query from donors. That architecture separates response replication, path-space resolution, and donor uncertainty without creating a classical inverse problem.
project_justification.fill: The project places finite-cohort identification under maintained cross-date average transport, an exact raw-estimator weighted-panel coefficient representation, estimation, conditional inference, and every least-favorable channel inside a single joint panel-law class. It derives the arbitrary-growth phase diagram, proves higher-smoothness donor saturation, and constructs a total covariance-aware local-polynomial interval with retained-block, event, and donor uncertainty calibrated separately.

body.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the causal financial-panel setup and show why volatility mismatch makes buy-and-hold effects harder than linear cumulative returns; their result informs the maintained event-transport identification layer rather than serving as a theorem-level target. Yan, Yao, and Zhou (2023, revised 2025) provide repeated-measurement Holder rates and a sparse-to-dense decomposition, while Gaiffas (2007) provides the pointwise random-design local-mass template. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) analyze generated coordinates attached to every training observation; Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) analyze replicated classical coordinate error requiring deconvolution. Those observation experiments inform the sigma-field distinction here. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closest conditional synthetic-control uncertainty decomposition and beta-mixing block coupling. Chen and Christensen (2015) provide weak-dependence Gram-matrix control for higher-order sieve regression. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) provide the ordered-modulus language for honest expected length. Ferman (2021) supplies the many-period--many-control motivation for retaining arbitrary relative growth. Shi et al. (2026) identify synthetic controls through predetermined donor proxies but do not study generated-proxy minimax behavior.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The two-sided local modulus is maintained rather than derived for the whole Holder ball. It is non-vacuous for nonzero standardized gradients when \(\lambda>1\) and asymmetric cusps when \(0<\lambda\le1\), but flat surfaces lie outside the donor lower-bound subclass. Identification remains conditional on the maintained cross-date cohort-average event-transport equality; historical placebo stability can challenge it but cannot verify it at the treated event date. The mean-only nonidentification proposition concerns the restricted map \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\); the full historical wealth panel can distinguish its witness laws and remains identifying under event transport.
body.honest_scope: The order frontier, positive-probability joint-law embedding, exact raw-estimator FWL identity, finite-cohort DID reduction, higher-order moving-center stability, covariance feasibility, and conditional expected-length result are all to be proved. All identification, risk, and interval claims remain conditional on the maintained cohort-average event-transport equality. The \(N^{-\min\{\lambda,1\}}\) donor converse remains conditional on \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}, which is assumed rather than derived from the Holder ball. The field-tier contribution is the positive-probability joint causal-panel lower-bound embedding, exact raw-estimator FWL representation, higher-smoothness generated-center saturation, and feasible honest expected-length frontier. Smoothness adaptation and sharp phase-intersection constants are inherited future work from the banked predecessor and are not contributions of this proposal. The proposal does not claim event-date exchangeability, identification from mean-only return matching, growing \(S\), or growing \(p(H+1)\).
